clue.text: Officer varied claim for reparation

indicators.note: reparation means repair, so the words before it are to be put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A claim for compensation has been put in several different forms by an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reparation' looks like the purpose of the claim, but it signals that VARIED CLAIM is rebuilt into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice admiral is a senior naval officer, ranking just below a full admiral.

clue.text: Tank — primarily, vehicle, armoured, turreted

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A description of a military tank as an armoured, turreted vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large tank or tub for holding liquids, as in brewing.

clue.text: Noble judge

definitions.meaning: a European nobleman of rank roughly equal to a British earl

explanation.definitionFit: A count is a foreign nobleman, and to count something is to consider or judge it so.

clue.text: Agree to move around a couple of pawns to start with

indicators.note: these words place the pair of pawns at the front, ahead of the roaming part

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn, so two of them give PP
to rove is to wander or move around

explanation.surface: A chess player consents to begin by advancing two pawns.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like chess opening advice; 'to start with' puts the pawns ahead of the wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve a plan is to agree to it or sanction it.

clue.text: Form of golf providing light entertain — ment

parts.note: a match is something used to give a light
a play is a piece of entertainment staged in a theatre

explanation.surface: A kind of golf that offers some gentle amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in 'entertain — ment' is a line break from the printed page: the word is 'entertainment'. 'light' looks like an adjective but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Match play is a golf format scored by holes won rather than total strokes.

clue.text: In a repeat performance, sailors cover river running north

indicators.note: the sailors cover the river, so their letters go around it

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, a common abbreviation for sailors

indicators.note: in a down clue, running north means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Naval men in a repeat show sing about a northbound river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running north' reverses the river in this down clue, giving ERU, and 'cover' means the sailors go around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeated showing of a programme or performance.

clue.text: Lamb under high ball — a bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this piece follows below the other

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high into the air
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A lamb grazes beneath a ball lofted high into the air, and someone makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' suggests a mistake but means a flowering plant; 'Lamb' is the writer, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden plant grown for its flowers, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: Rotten start

explanation.definitionFit: Milk that has gone bad is off, and the start of a race is the off.

clue.text: One who's experienced a lot, without men in their later years around

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece is put on the outside of another
repeats that the later-years word goes round the men

parts.note: people in their later years are older
a stag party is a gathering for men only, so stag can stand for men

explanation.surface: A seasoned person spends their old age with no men around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside', backed up by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran, someone long practised in some activity.

clue.text: Marker upset flanker, with two companions involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside, so the companions go into the rearranged word
upset means knocked over, so the letters of the word next to it are rearranged

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order, so two give CHCH

explanation.surface: A rugby wing forward is knocked over, with two team-mates caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the rugby forward into FRENALK, and 'involved' puts the companions inside it. A flanker is a rugby forward.
explanation.definitionFit: French chalk is a soft talc used by tailors to mark cloth.

clue.text: Bird who sends out signals?

definitions.meaning: a swan, and also a South American bird, both named for their call
a bugler who sounds calls on a brass instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter is both a kind of swan or crane-like bird and a person who plays calls on a trumpet.

clue.text: Move leader of grockles into Cornish resort

indicators.note: one piece is put into the middle of the resort's name

parts.note: Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Get the first of the tourists to go into a Cornish seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Grockles is West Country slang for tourists, apt for Bude, a resort on the Cornish coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to move slightly, usually in a negative such as 'it won't budge'.

clue.text: Early centre of Christianity, opposed to old church

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

explanation.surface: An early seat of the Christian faith that stands against the old church.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch in Syria was where followers of Jesus were first called Christians.

clue.text: Blanket is brown in this republic

parts.note: an afghan is a knitted or crocheted woollen blanket
taken as written
tan is a yellowish-brown colour

explanation.surface: In one republic the blankets are brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghanistan is an Islamic republic in Central Asia, so the clue's 'this republic' points to it.

clue.text: Nothing relating to ears or to languages

definitions.note: the definition borrows 'relating' from earlier: relating to certain languages, an adjective

parts.note: nil means nothing or zero
otic is the anatomical adjective for the ear

explanation.surface: A word that means nothing to do with ears, or else something about languages.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition shares 'relating' with the wordplay, so it reads 'relating to languages'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic describes the peoples of the Nile region and the language group they speak.

clue.text: Triangular brickwork produced by film star

definitions.meaning: the triangular upper wall at the end of a pitched roof
Clark ..., Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind

explanation.definitionFit: A gable is the triangular end wall under a roof, and Clark Gable was a famous film actor.

clue.text: Take a butcher's around capital

indicators.note: around suggests moving the letters about into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Take a look around the city, in cockney fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a butcher's' is rhyming slang for take a look (butcher's hook), which disguises the fodder: A BUTCHERS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania.

clue.text: Slow cooking required for the garlic

indicators.note: cooking means being worked on or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Slow cooking is what the garlic needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow cooking' reads as one phrase, but 'Slow' is the definition and 'cooking' rearranges THE GARLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and drowsy, lacking energy, so slow-moving.

clue.text: To call up the rank and file first is impractical

indicators.note: first places the rank and file ahead of the summoning word

parts.note: taken as written
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means this word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to summon or call, as to a court

explanation.surface: Summoning the ordinary soldiers before anyone else is not a practical idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the summoning word into ETIC in this down clue; 'first' puts the soldiers before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretic means concerned with theory rather than practice, so not practical.

clue.text: Original model they recap incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly means wrongly arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: They sum up the original design wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original pattern from which copies are made.

clue.text: Tombstone finally acquired an epitaph — a boost for self-esteem

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: got means acquired or obtained
RIP, rest in peace, is a classic epitaph on a gravestone

explanation.surface: A gravestone finally gets an inscription, which flatters the deceased's vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done chiefly to make oneself feel important.

clue.text: In Mediterranean area, second year gets backing of first class

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so this piece is read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A second year in the Mediterranean is supported by a top-class performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) appears as AI, which 'backing of' turns into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a country on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Newspaper column that sheds a bit of light

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a beam, like a column of light, is a shaft

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature that is illuminating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper column' suggests a regular article; in fact it is SUN (the tabloid) plus BEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a single ray of sunlight, a small shaft of light.

clue.text: To sum up, I had put tree in the wrong way round

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: the wrong way round means this word is read backwards

parts.note: the rowan is the mountain ash tree

explanation.surface: In summary, someone planted a tree back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' reverses the tree into NAWOR, and 'in' puts it inside the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: In a word is an idiom meaning briefly or in summary.

clue.text: Two states with river scenery

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware
CO is the postal abbreviation for Colorado

explanation.surface: Two US states and a river make a fine landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the stage setting or scenery of a theatrical production.

clue.text: Managed to fire rifle

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
to sack is to fire someone from a job

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in firing a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' and 'rifle' suggest guns; 'rifle' is the verb meaning to search through.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it hurriedly to steal, which is what ransacking means.

clue.text: Courts in which a case is inconclusive

indicators.note: inconclusive means lacking an ending, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

explanation.surface: Courts where a case ends without a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' suggests law courts, which the inconclusive case supports, but it means courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courts in Roman houses or modern buildings.

clue.text: Part of South Eire belonging to them

indicators.note: part of means only some letters of the following words are used, running across them

explanation.surface: A piece of southern Ireland belongs to those people.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive form meaning of or belonging to them.

clue.text: Be sick — get medical man in to effect cure in church

parts.note: cat is British slang meaning to vomit

indicators.note: the doctor is put inside the curing word

parts.note: to heal is to bring about a cure
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Feeling ill, get a doctor in to cure you in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be sick' uses old British slang for vomiting; 'in' puts the doctor inside the curing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, holding the bishop's throne.

clue.text: Air bed

definitions.meaning: a tune or song, especially a ballad
a layer or stratum, as in a bed of oysters

explanation.definitionFit: A lay is a song or ballad, and also a layer or bed, as of oysters.

clue.text: Somebody obsessed with teachers

definitions.meaning: a fanatic or enthusiast, as in a fitness fanatic
the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union, by its initials

explanation.definitionFit: A nut is a fanatic for something, and the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain.

clue.text: Break up celebration, getting shot of first of your guests (4,7) 23,196

indicators.note: getting shot of means getting rid of, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a party is a celebration

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: company means guests, as in having company

explanation.surface: A party is broken up after the first guests leave.
explanation.walkthrough: '23,196 (11)' at the end is the puzzle number picked up from the printed page, not part of the clue. Y leaves PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: To part company is to separate or break up a relationship.
